name: Cursor
summary: An editor-first AI coding environment with agentic IDE workflows, rules, memories, MCP, and cursor-agent CLI support.
overview: Cursor is an AI-native code editor and agent environment where the main interaction happens inside the IDE, with cursor-agent extending some workflows into the terminal. It should be described as an editor-first Agent: project rules, memories, MCP configuration, code navigation, and inline editing are more important than a standalone skill marketplace. Its value on 2playclaw.com is helping users decide when an IDE-native agent beats a terminal-first agent.

strengths.title: Editor-native interaction
strengths.body: Useful when the user wants agent help while staying in the same environment used to read, edit, navigate, and review code.

strengths.title: Rules and memories
strengths.body: Cursor Rules, User Rules, and memories provide persistent context that can shape agent behavior across files and projects.

strengths.title: MCP across editor and CLI
strengths.body: Cursor documents MCP support for external tools and data sources, with CLI support for cursor-agent as well.

strengths.title: Lower switching cost
strengths.body: The IDE-first surface is good for developers who want fast iteration, codebase navigation, and agent assistance without leaving the editor.

extensionModel.label: Rules
extensionModel.body: Rules are Cursor's main reusable-instruction layer for controlling behavior at user and project scope.

extensionModel.label: MCP
extensionModel.body: Cursor supports MCP for external tools, resources, prompts, and roots.

extensionModel.label: CLI
extensionModel.body: cursor-agent can run from the terminal and use MCP servers configured for the workflow.

extensionModel.label: Workflow
extensionModel.body: Workflow content usually appears as rules, prompts, project conventions, and tool combinations rather than as a single skill format.

recommendedStacks.title: Project rules baseline
recommendedStacks.body: Use Cursor with reviewed rule packs and repository-specific guidance for consistent code generation and review behavior.

recommendedStacks.title: Editor plus external context
recommendedStacks.body: Pair Cursor with MCP tools for documentation lookup, browser verification, database context, or product-system access.

recommendedStacks.title: IDE-first adoption path
recommendedStacks.body: Recommend Cursor when teams want agentic coding but prefer editor interaction over command-line sessions.

limitations: Cursor rules are powerful but can become stale or overly broad if teams do not curate them.
Do not treat every generic skill or prompt pack as Cursor-compatible unless it explicitly maps to rules, MCP, or cursor-agent usage.
Editor support and cursor-agent CLI support should be labeled separately.
Community rule repositories need review before being recommended publicly.
